meta.title: MSS 2026-2035 Strategic Intelligence Portal
meta.subtitle: Interactive Strategy Matrix Explorer
meta.vision: To position Malaysia as a trusted, innovative and future-ready standardisation leader that enables a high-value, sustainable, digitally connected and globally competitive economy.
meta.mission: To deliver a focused, coordinated and globally aligned standards ecosystem that translates national priorities into measurable productivity, safety, sustainability and global influence outcomes.
meta.source: V4 Malaysian Standardisation Strategy 2026 Formatting.pdf, Section 7.4 to 7.11
meta.logic_chain: Gap → Pillar → Domain → Initiative → Outcome → KPI → 2035 Target

P1.name: Strategic Prioritisation & National Competitiveness
P1.gap: G1 - Uneven Standardisation Priority and Intensity Across Sectors
P1.core_question: Which standards matter most for Malaysia's competitiveness, public interest and future growth?
P1.summary: Pillar 1 aligns the Malaysian Standards pipeline with national priorities such as RMK-13, NIMP 2030, NETR, DAN 2.0, the Halal Industry Master Plan, the National Semiconductor Strategy and AI Nation 2030.

P2.name: Digital & Intelligent Standards Ecosystem
P2.gap: G2 - Limited Impact Measurement and Performance Intelligence
P2.core_question: How can Malaysia digitally manage, monitor and measure the standards lifecycle?
P2.summary: Pillar 2 builds the digital backbone for standards through DSIS, MySOL integration, lifecycle analytics, machine-readable standards and SCPI.

P3.name: Regulatory Coordination & Conformity Ecosystem
P3.gap: G3 - Uneven Regulatory Embedding and Cross-Agency Coordination
P3.core_question: How can regulators reference and apply Malaysian Standards consistently?
P3.summary: Pillar 3 strengthens regulator coordination, regulatory citation, conformity pathways, Refer-or-Explain and the National Conformity Mark.

P4.name: Industry Adoption & Inclusive Participation
P4.gap: G4 - Weak Adoption and Compliance Pathways
P4.core_question: How can standards be made practical, affordable and usable by firms and society?
P4.summary: Pillar 4 supports MSMEs, online sellers, smallholders and industry through adoption vouchers, Standard-in-a-Box, SOSSAP, consortia and expert support.

P5.name: Agile Governance & Future-Ready Standards
P5.gap: G5 - Limited Governance Agility and Capacity Constraints
P5.core_question: How can the standards system move faster in emerging and fast-changing sectors?
P5.summary: Pillar 5 introduces fast-track standards, regulatory sandbox models, AI-assisted tools and a National Expert Pool.

P6.name: International Leadership & Global Positioning
P6.gap: G6 - Limited International Alignment, Leadership and Agenda-Setting Participation
P6.core_question: How can Malaysia move from standards taker to selective global standards leader?
P6.summary: Pillar 6 concentrates Malaysia's global leadership in areas such as halal, rubber, palm oil sustainability, tropical biosecurity, hydrogen, environment, circular economy and digital trust.
